Lexington Living: A polished, history-minded magazine for Lexington's established, highly educated and affluent homeowners. Readers are physicians, professors, executives and long-time families who value the town's Revolutionary heritage, top-ranked schools and quiet civic life. Tone: refined, thoughtful and well-informed. Design: generous white space, elegant serif headlines, restrained palette and large editorial photography. Copy leans toward profiles, preservation, schools and arts. Best advertisers: private wealth and estate planning, architects and builders, fine dining, galleries, boutique services.
MetroWest Living: A broad, energetic regional title for the commuter belt west of Boston: young families, first-time buyers, tech and biotech professionals and a diverse mix of long-time residents and newcomers across many towns. Readers are busy and practical, and they scan more than they read. Tone: friendly, upbeat and useful. Design: bold, colourful, modular layouts with short blocks of copy, strong calls to action and plenty of event calendars and guides. Copy favours things to do, school and youth sports news, local deals and how-tos. Best advertisers: restaurants, family services, home improvement, fitness, auto, healthcare and retail.
Westwood Living: A warm, residential magazine for quiet, family-centred neighbourhoods of single-family homes, cul-de-sacs and school-run routines. A solid middle-to-upper-middle income readership where parents, coaches and PTA volunteers are the community's backbone. Tone: neighbourly, wholesome and reassuring. Design: clean, bright and approachable, with rounded accents, candid community photos and clear hierarchy. Copy favours school honours, youth sports, town meetings, volunteers and seasonal events. Best advertisers: pediatric and family dental, tutoring, real estate agents, landscapers, home services, local eateries.
Swampscott Neighbors: A casual, close-knit seaside community newsletter with a mixed-demographic readership: multi-generation locals, retirees, young couples and working families who share beaches, a small downtown and a strong sense of place. Value-conscious readers who trust word of mouth. Tone: chatty, humorous and personal, with a blue-collar warmth. Design: friendly and slightly retro, with coastal blues, bold local photography, and busy community boards and classifieds. Copy favours harbour and beach news, high-school teams, fundraisers, small-business spotlights and community notices. Best advertisers: neighbourhood restaurants, trades, hair and barber shops, marine and seasonal businesses, local services.
Weston Neighbors: A discreet, upscale publication for Weston's large-lot estates, private-club memberships and long-established wealth. A small but very affluent and privacy-minded readership that values excellent schools, conservation land, horse and equestrian culture and understated luxury. Tone: composed, sophisticated and quietly confident, never flashy. Design: luxurious restraint, with a muted palette, large-format imagery, fine typography and ample margins. Copy favours land and conservation, philanthropy, the arts, private education and refined living. Best advertisers: luxury real estate, wealth managers, custom builders and landscape architects, concierge healthcare, high-end automotive and travel.
